solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Noble returned to tour a Boer encampment?

indicators.note: to tour is to go all the way round, so the reversed noble word surrounds the a
returned means the word for noble is read back to front

parts.note: noble in the sense of regal, kingly

explanation.surface: An aristocrat, back from abroad, is taken round a settlers' camp in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REGAL into LAGER, and 'to tour' puts A inside it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans word for a defensive camp ringed by wagons, as used by Boer trekkers.

clue.text: Like having to remain outside, being loyal

indicators.note: outside says the remain word goes round the like letters

parts.note: to lie is to remain, as in lie fallow
eg, for example, means like or such as

explanation.surface: Staying out of doors while staying faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege man owed loyal feudal service to his lord, hence faithful.

clue.text: One may follow this river northwards when in control

indicators.note: when in places the reversed river inside the control word

parts.note: to guide is to steer or control

indicators.note: northwards in a down clue means the river is read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is the African river

explanation.surface: A boatman in charge sails north up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses NILE to ELIN; the Nile does flow north, a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or recommendation is something people are expected to follow.

clue.text: Weed mainly grows wild in desert

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the desert word

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray

indicators.note: wild says the trimmed letters are scrambled
mainly drops the last letter of grows

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A weed that mostly grows wild in arid land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun for dry land but is the verb rat; 'mainly' drops the final S before 'wild' scrambles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered plant toxic to livestock, a notorious pest on grazing land.

clue.text: Scots man in a depression shows caution

indicators.note: in places the Scots word inside the depression word

parts.note: a dish is a hollow or shallow depression
mon is the Scottish dialect form of man

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stuck in a hollow behaves warily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word; the definition is the verb 'caution'.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone is to warn or reprove them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Thermal control system indicating Orion has shifted

indicators.note: has shifted says the letters of the two words are moved about

explanation.surface: A stargazer's gadget showing that the constellation Orion has moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment that cools and regulates a building's air temperature.

clue.text: Brief note about to introduce bishop's service, as called for?

indicators.note: to introduce says about comes before the bishop letter
brief says the note word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a minim is a musical note
CA, for circa, means about
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A short message about bringing in the bishop's church service, as requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks ecclesiastical but means a taxi company you phone for.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a private hire car booked by phone, a service called for.

clue.text: Nationality of old PM that hasn't died

indicators.note: that hasn't says the died letter is missing from the PM

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: Asking the nationality of a former prime minister who is still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the state in the Middle East holds this nationality.

clue.text: Male wrapping up inferior display left by women — good luck with this?

indicators.note: wrapping up puts the male word round what remains

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: left by says the women letters depart from the inferior display

parts.note: worse means inferior
a show is a display
W is women, so two Ws for the plural

explanation.surface: A man covering up a poor show the ladies walked out of, wished good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'women' supplies two Ws, one from each of the inferior and display words, which 'left by' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron hung over a door is a traditional token of good fortune.

clue.text: Dropping English books into bottom of bag

parts.note: B is book, so BB is books
into gives IN, its shortened form

indicators.note: bottom of points to the final letter of the word bag

explanation.surface: Someone drops English books into the bottom of a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide that is ebbing is falling or dropping, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Supplier runs into animals I missed

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside what remains
missed says the letter I is left out of the animals

parts.note: reindeer are animals (the plural form is the same)
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A provider charges into a herd of animals, but somebody missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' removes the I from REINDEER, leaving RENDEER, and 'into' places R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To render is to give or provide, so one who renders is a provider.

clue.text: Religious image of maiden in cowl briefly put on city church

indicators.note: put on says the next part is set after the city and church letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in puts the maiden letter inside the shortened cowl word
briefly cuts the last letter off the cowl word

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A painting of a girl in a monk's hood is hung on a cathedral in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' turns HOOD into HOO, and 'in' places M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'behold the man', it names paintings of Christ crowned with thorns.

clue.text: Hold together present company with new order

indicators.note: with new order says the clue's present-then-company sequence is swapped round

parts.note: present as in being here, not away

explanation.surface: Keep the firm in one piece, present company included, under a reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together as a unified whole, said of parts or of an argument.

clue.text: Dependent upon extra court pursuing one on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside says those letters sit within the extra word

parts.note: added means extra, additional

indicators.note: pursuing puts the court letters after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A defendant relies on extra time in court with an insider's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a drug or habit is reliant on it.

clue.text: A source of hot water, one known for firing up plant

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring, often hot

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the businessman's name is read upwards

parts.note: Lord Sugar, host of the UK version of The Apprentice, is famous for saying 'You're fired'

explanation.surface: A hot spring and a man who sacks people, in a firing kiln setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sugar is a British tycoon whose TV catchphrase is 'You're fired!'; 'up' reverses SUGAR to RAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable whose young spears are eaten; it is a perennial garden crop.

clue.text: Party crashed by regulars in unlit bar

indicators.note: crashed by says those letters break into the party word

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

indicators.note: regulars in takes every other letter of the word unlit

explanation.surface: A party in a dark pub is gatecrashed by its regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'unlit' are N and I, which go inside BASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude or expel them, a synonym.

clue.text: Enter, if it moves the queen

indicators.note: moves says the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to come in, provided the monarch makes a move.
explanation.definitionFit: Wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, the famous Egyptian queen of the bust in Berlin.

clue.text: Problem surrounding university, one assumes?

indicators.note: surrounding puts the problem word round the university letter

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a university that someone takes for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'assumes' meaning puts on airs rather than supposes.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off assumes, that is adopts, an affected manner or pose.

clue.text: After stoppage of play, intially fled over pitch

indicators.note: after says fled follows those first letters
initially (misspelt in the clue) takes the first letters of the three words before it

parts.note: ran means fled
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: After play was halted, someone fled across the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the cricket field but means a vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice is a range of musical pitch.

clue.text: Italian footballer concerned with making a comeback — he hasn't scored for years

parts.note: Paolo Rossi was Italy's striker in their 1982 World Cup win

indicators.note: making a comeback says the concerned word is turned back to front

parts.note: in means involved in or concerned with

explanation.surface: An Italian striker returns to the game after years without a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' refers to writing music, not goals: the composer died long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barber of Seville composer is long dead, so he has written no score for ages.

clue.text: Pause a jazz song

definitions.meaning: an idiom for taking a short break from work
the Dave Brubeck Quartet's famous 1959 jazz piece in 5/4 time

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means take a short rest, and it is also the title of Brubeck's jazz standard.

clue.text: Know to make cladding for pine room

indicators.note: cladding for says the know word covers the pine word

parts.note: ken is knowledge or to know, Scots usage
to itch for something is to long or pine for it

explanation.surface: Carpentry advice on fitting pine panelling to a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like timber but means yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a house where meals are cooked is a room.

clue.text: Mixture of flour and fat vegetables said to make money

indicators.note: said signals that the two cooking words, spoken, give the answer's sound

parts.words: Mixture of flour and fat vegetables
parts.note: a roux is flour cooked in butter or fat as a sauce base; peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: A cooking scene: roux and vegetables combine to make a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency units of India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are a form of money.

clue.text: Rest after month in France avoiding a disturbance

indicators.note: after puts the rest word following the shortened month
avoiding says the letter a is left out of the French month

parts.note: aout is French for August
taken as written
a break is a rest

explanation.surface: Taking a holiday after August in France to escape trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden eruption of violence or disease is a disturbance.

clue.text: Credit card, finally found in market abroad, returned

indicators.note: returned says the whole thing is read upwards
found in puts that letter inside the market word

parts.note: a souk is an Arab marketplace

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word card

explanation.surface: A credit card lost in a foreign bazaar is handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige or praise for an achievement; credit in the sense of honour.

clue.text: Armed force OK to be included in US soldier's mural?

indicators.note: to be included in places the two pieces inside the soldier letters

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
RAF is the Royal Air Force
fit means OK, healthy

explanation.surface: Permission for the air force to join an American soldier's wall painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that graffiti is only loosely a mural.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted or scrawled writing on a wall counts, with a wink, as wall art.

clue.text: Praised woman going about with one left out

indicators.note: out says one left letter is dropped
going about means the woman's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Delilah is the biblical woman who betrayed Samson
L is the abbreviation for left, here just one of them

explanation.surface: A woman gets admiration as she goes around, someone being excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' turns DELILAH into HALILED, and 'out' removes one of its two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim or greet them enthusiastically.

clue.text: Head's extremely smug about smacking

indicators.note: about says those outer letters go round the head word
extremely takes the outer letters of the word smug

parts.note: noggin is slang for the head; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied headteacher is caught administering corporal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smacking' looks like a beating but means a loud kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking kiss is a loud one, so kissing passionately matches smacking.

clue.text: Negative MPs shouted out cries from the Shires?

indicators.note: shouted out tells you to go by the sound of the voters' word

parts.note: the nays are the MPs voting no in a division

explanation.surface: Rural Tory backbenchers shouting their opposition in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Shires are big Shire horses, a British draught breed, not the English counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses' calls are whinnies, and Shire horses make them.
